transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because lately I just can’t keep my head clear, especially at work. I’m a therapist, so I’m supposed to be really present with people, you know, tracking what they’re saying and remembering the thread of things, but I keep losing it. Like a client will be talking and I’ll realize I’ve missed part of what they said, or I’ll have to work really hard to piece it back together.

And then with chart notes, I’ll read the same note over and over and it’s like the words are there but they’re not sticking. It takes me way longer than it should. Even simple decisions I used to make without thinking—like how to phrase something in a note, or what to do next in a session—I just kind of freeze. It’s embarrassing, honestly, and it’s starting to feel like I can’t trust my own head the way I used to.
Can you tell me how you’ve been feeling emotionally lately—have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say it’s all one thing, but I’ve definitely lost interest in stuff that used to feel like… me, I guess.

Like my guitar is just sitting in the corner of my room. I used to pick it up without even thinking—just mess around for ten minutes or learn part of a song—and now I look at it and it feels like this weird obligation, so I don’t touch it. Same with soccer. I keep saying I’m going to go, and then when it gets close I bail, or I make some excuse, but honestly it’s not even that I have a good reason. I just can’t get myself to care enough to show up.

And I volunteer at the shelter sometimes, or I did, and I’ve been canceling that too, which makes me feel awful because that’s something I actually believe in. But even that feels like this heavy thing now. Cooking, hiking—things I used to do to feel grounded—if I try, it’s like I’m just going through the motions. I can make the food or walk the trail, but there’s no satisfaction in it. It just feels kind of pointless, like I’m doing the shape of the activity without any of the feeling that used to come with it.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the time, nearly every day, rather than just having moments of feeling this way?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. It’s not like I’m consciously thinking, “I’m depressed,” every minute of the day, if that makes sense. I don’t always have a clear label for it.

But there is this… heaviness, I guess, that’s around a lot. Some days it’s more obvious, and some days I’m just kind of moving through things and only realize later that I felt low the whole time. I don’t know if it’s “most of the time” in the way you mean clinically, but it’s definitely more than just a bad hour here or there. It feels like it’s become the background, not just a passing mood.
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or that you're lacking energy more often than usual?

Yeah… definitely. It’s kind of hard to explain because it’s not just “I’m sleepy,” exactly. It’s more like everything takes this ridiculous amount of effort now.

Even really small stuff—like showering in the morning, or getting myself dressed, or driving over to the clinic—feels like I’m dragging around a backpack full of bricks. Like I can do it, technically, but the whole time there’s this resistance, like my body and brain are both saying, “Why is this so hard?” And by the time I get to paperwork, even if it’s not complicated, it feels like I’m pushing through mud. I’ll sit there trying to finish notes and it’s like the energy just drains out of me before I’ve even really started.

It’s frustrating because these are normal parts of my day. They shouldn’t feel like big tasks. But lately they do.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… I think so. I didn’t really clock it at first because it wasn’t like I made a decision to eat less or anything. It’s more like I just don’t get hungry the way I normally would.

Most days, I’ll kind of go through the morning and then a big part of the afternoon and realize I haven’t eaten, but only because someone says something like, “Did you have lunch?” or asks if I want food. And then I’m like… oh, I guess I didn’t. It’s not that food sounds disgusting exactly, it’s just not registering as something I want or need unless it’s pointed out to me.

And I’ve noticed my pants are looser, which feels weird to say out loud, but yeah. Like I’m having to pull them up more, or they don’t sit the same. I haven’t been trying to lose weight. I think I’ve just been skipping meals without really meaning to.
Would you say that most days, you're feeling down or low for most of the day, rather than just having brief moments of feeling that way?

I’m honestly not sure how to measure it exactly. Like, I don’t know if I could say, “Yes, it’s most of the day every day,” in a precise way, because I’m not always checking in with myself. A lot of the time I’m just trying to get through whatever I’m doing, and then afterward I realize I’ve been in this low place for hours.

It’s definitely not just quick little moments, though. It’s more like… it hangs around. Sometimes it’s in the front of my mind, where I really feel it, and other times it’s more muted, like background noise, but it’s still there. So I guess if you’re asking whether it’s more than brief waves, then yeah, it feels more persistent than that. I just don’t know how confidently to call it “most of the day.”
Would you say that your low mood has lasted most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think if I’m being honest, it’s been at least that long. Probably more like about a month now.

It sort of started after the clinic lost some staff and everything got rearranged. My schedule shifted into more late-evening coverage, and I ended up with a lot heavier crisis paperwork than before. At first I kept telling myself it was just the schedule change, like, of course I’d feel off because my routine got thrown and I was staying later. But it didn’t really let up. It’s been this ongoing low feeling that’s just kind of followed me through most days since then.

I don’t know if every single day has been exactly the same, but for the past month, yeah, it’s been there nearly every day, and usually for a lot of the day.
Have you found yourself feeling like a failure or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even when it might not make sense?

Yeah… definitely. More than I want to admit, probably.

It’s like, if I miss one detail in a note, even something small, or if I don’t return a call right away, my brain just goes straight to, “You’re useless. You’re not doing enough. You’re letting people down.” And it doesn’t really matter if there’s a reasonable explanation, like I was busy or had back-to-back things going on. I still end up replaying it over and over.

Especially at the clinic, because I know the clients are depending on us, and everyone else is already stretched thin. So if I forget something or I’m even a little late following up, it feels way bigger than it probably is. I start thinking I’m failing the clients, and failing the team, and that everyone would be better off if I could just get it together.

I know on some level that missing one detail doesn’t mean I’m a terrible person, but it doesn’t feel that way in the moment. It feels like proof that I’m not capable.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, even when you make yourself do them?

Yeah… yeah, I have. That’s actually been one of the weirder parts, because I keep thinking if I just do the things I normally like, I’ll feel more like myself again, but it doesn’t really work that way.

Like my guitar has just been sitting in the corner. I used to pick it up without even thinking about it, even if it was only for ten minutes, and now I’ll look at it and think, “I should play,” and then it just feels like this whole task. Or I’ll pick it up and strum a little, and it’s not unpleasant exactly, but there’s no spark to it. I’m not getting that feeling of getting pulled into it.

And I’ve been bailing on soccer more than I want to admit. I’ll tell myself I’m too tired or it’s too much to get there, but if I’m honest, part of it is that I don’t really want to go. Same with the shelter. I used to feel like that mattered to me in a way I could really feel, and now I keep backing out or putting it off, and then I feel bad about that too.

Even stuff that should be nice, like cooking something decent or going hiking, I can make myself do it sometimes, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Like I’m doing the activity because it’s technically something I enjoy, but I’m not actually enjoying it. It just feels kind of flat and pointless.

inference_history.note: The patient's reported loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, emotional flatness, and cognitive difficulties align more strongly with depressive disorders. This narrows the focus from broader differential candidates like anxiety, dissociative symptoms, personality factors, and neurocognitive issues. Major Depressive Disorder (single or recurrent episode) and Neurotic Depression remain plausible.

The patient described persistent low mood, anhedonia, and functional impairment in cognitive domains (e.g., concentration, decision-making) that align with depressive symptomatology. The chronicity and background nature of the mood disturbance suggest a possibility of persistent rather than episodic depression. No features of panic, obsessions, trauma, or mania were endorsed, which reduces likelihood of other major categories like anxiety disorders, OCD, PTSD, or bipolar disorder. Further clarification of duration and course is needed to differentiate between F32.9 and F33.9.

The patient has confirmed that the low mood has lasted for at least the past month, nearly every day, and persists for most of the day. This supports the criteria for major depressive disorder, and the distinction between F32.9 (major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified) and F33.9 (major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified) remains dependent on history of prior episodes, which has not yet been clarified. No further ruling out has occurred at this turn.
